tasks.title: Integration test: two generations between two status calls

details.goal: Prove with real published files that `status.graph.size_bytes` is the size the reader opened, for an accepted swap, for a publish that lands after the open, and for a refused newer-schema swap where the old reader keeps serving.
steps: Add the `PublishOptions` interface and the fourth parameter to the existing `publish` helper (`:106-136`), with the two conditional `upsertMeta` writes inside the existing transaction.
Add the `PAD` constant and the `graphSize(ctx)` helper, merge `statSync` into the `node:fs` import on `:3`, and add the `handle` and `type ToolContext` imports.
Add case 1: the accepted swap, then a third publish after the refresh, asserting the context keeps the size it opened.
Add case 2: the newer-schema padded copy, the refusal, and the served size still reported beside a larger file on disk.
Extend the file docstring (`:14-30`): its case list is `:19-22`, so add the served-size coverage to that list rather than to the constants below the docstring.
Run the checks below.

tasks.title: Update GitHub issue #13 with the shipped fix

details.goal: Record the shipped fix on https://github.com/Alfar-Lab/sangkar-mcp/issues/13 so the issue is answered in place instead of being closed off-list: one comment carrying the commit, the changed files, the two acceptance criteria with their evidence, and the tests that pin them; then close the issue only if both criteria are demonstrated.
details.contract:
This task owns no repository file and must not modify one: its only writes are a GitHub comment and, when warranted, the issue state. Do not edit the issue body, title, labels, milestones or any earlier comment.
The comment must carry, in this order: `git rev-parse --short HEAD` and `git show --stat --oneline HEAD`; the two acceptance criteria quoted from the issue body, each followed by the observed evidence (for criterion 1: `status`, `summary` and `expand` on one generation with the numbers actually read; for criterion 2: the test name and its assertion, plus `tests/store-refresh.test.ts`'s refused-swap case); the before/after `status.payload.graph` excerpt (before the fix the payload paired a served generation's `nodes` with the size of a file the reader never opened — reproduced as `nodes: 11` beside `size_bytes: 720896` for a 172032-byte opened file); and the commands run with their pass/fail counts.
Post the body from a file (`gh issue comment 13 --repo Alfar-Lab/sangkar-mcp --body-file <path>`), never as a shell-quoted inline `--body`: the text contains backticks, quotes and JSON, and an inline body mangles them.
Close the issue only when both criteria are quoted as satisfied in that same comment: `gh issue close 13 --repo Alfar-Lab/sangkar-mcp --comment "Fixed in <sha>: ..."`. If any criterion is unmet, leave the issue open and name the unmet one in the comment instead.
Forbidden: `git push --force`, tags, `npm publish`, edits to any repository file, and any change to the issue's body or labels.
steps: Confirm the phase gate is green and `git status --porcelain` is clean apart from the plan directories; record `git rev-parse --short HEAD`.
Write the comment body to `/tmp/gh13-comment.md` with the contract's content, quoting both acceptance criteria from `gh issue view 13 --repo Alfar-Lab/sangkar-mcp --json body`.
Post it with `gh issue comment 13 --repo Alfar-Lab/sangkar-mcp --body-file /tmp/gh13-comment.md` and record the returned issue URL.

Close only if both criteria are demonstrated: `gh issue close 13 --repo Alfar-Lab/sangkar-mcp --comment "Fixed in <sha>: graph.size_bytes now reports the size of the file the reader opened."` Otherwise report the unmet criterion and leave it open.
Delete the temp file and record the comment URL, the issue state and any unmet criterion in `progress`.
details.verify: Done when `gh issue view 13 --repo Alfar-Lab/sangkar-mcp --json state,comments` shows the new comment, the state is `CLOSED` (or the comment names the criterion that is still unmet and the state is `OPEN`), `git status --porcelain` matches the state recorded before this task, the temp file is deleted, and the comment URL is recorded in `progress`.
